stem: For an individual with significant dual sensory loss (deaf-blindness), which sensory input serves as the essential medium for receiving detailed interpersonal communication?

options.text: Enlarged print read at close range with high-power magnification.
options.rationale: High magnification still depends on usable vision, which significant dual sensory loss does not reliably provide.

options.text: A cochlear implant paired with an FM system to restore speech understanding.
options.rationale: Auditory devices can support awareness of sound, but they do not replace touch as the primary channel for complex communication in significant dual sensory loss.

options.text: Vibrotactile alerts that convert environmental sounds into distinct vibration patterns.
options.rationale: Vibrotactile alerts can signal sounds or events, but they do not carry the syntax and vocabulary needed for detailed interpersonal communication.

options.text: Tactile interaction through braille and tactile sign language for expressive and receptive communication.
options.rationale: Touch (tactile input) is the primary viable sensory channel for complex language and text when both vision and hearing are severely compromised.

explanation: Because deaf-blindness involves concurrent impairments in both vision and hearing, tactile modalities—such as tactile sign language, hands-on signing, and refreshable braille—provide the primary means for rich, expressive, and receptive communication.

references.title: National Center on Deafblindness: Overview on Deaf-Blindness
